lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé lacks a clear product target or career story.
items.because: The current mechanic role leaves recruiters unsure which direction you are pursuing.

items.says: The experience entries are not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: The 2024 Harbor Payments internship appears below Crestline Logistics, which ended in 2023.

items.says: The operations experience does not make its relevance to product decisions apparent.
items.because: The reader is left to connect the product-adjacent skills to product work.

items.says: Product credentials are concentrated in an internship and a student project.
items.because: Candidates for product roles may have more recent, full-time product experience.

items.says: Education may take too much space relative to experience.
items.because: The internship and project results are stronger evidence for product roles.

items.says: Check spacing and page length in the final document.
items.because: The text alone does not show whether the layout is readable.

items.says: Standardize date formatting and bullet punctuation.
items.because: Consistency helps polish the résumé.

items.says: Replace the contact details if they are placeholders.
items.because: Placeholder-style details can undermine credibility in an application.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA date indicates completion or expected completion.
items.because: The degree’s awarded status should not be ambiguous.

items.says: Make the mechanic role’s place in a product career path clear.
items.because: It could suggest that you are no longer pursuing product.

items.says: Make your individual role in the rebuilding work clear.
items.because: A product recruiter may otherwise see disconnected technical detail rather than operational ownership.

items.says: Define how the five-day dry-dock measure was calculated.
items.because: The turnaround result needs to be easy to understand.

items.says: Clarify the scale and significance of the inspection work.
items.because: The bullet gives little indication of the outcome or level of responsibility.

items.says: Show what decisions or results followed from the scorecards and meeting.
items.because: Saying the meeting discussed the scorecards is weak on its own.

items.says: Clarify the pick-error measurement period or baseline.
items.because: The 30% reduction needs measurement context.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the supervisors’ and pickers’ work.
items.because: The bullet credits a collaborative redesign and retraining effort.

items.says: Define and substantiate the forecast-error calculation.
items.because: The meaning and calculation of the result need to be defensible.

items.says: Show your specific role in establishing the consensus forecast.
items.because: The bullet does not make that contribution clear.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the many activities in the rollout bullet.
items.because: It is long and crowded, and competes with product experience for attention.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the rollout and related work.
items.because: The reader needs to understand what you owned.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 driver hours were measured.
items.because: The savings figure needs measurement context.

items.says: Explain what the verification change involved.
items.because: The onboarding result should be understandable.

items.says: Explain how the pilot population and median time were measured.
items.because: The result needs credible measurement context.

items.says: The checkout experiment is repeated in a later bullet.
items.because: The two bullets appear to describe the same A/B test rather than distinct achievements.

items.says: Define the ticket-based RICE Reach measure, including its population and timeframe.
items.because: Support-ticket volume may be a proxy, but readers may question whether it represents users reached.

items.says: Show what the dispute prioritization informed.
items.because: The bullet gives the scoring method without its decision outcome.

items.says: Clarify how the merchant research and loss sizing affected the decision.
items.because: The bullet does not explain their effect on the roadmap priority.

items.says: Distinguish this roadmap bullet from the preceding one.
items.because: They overlap and seem to claim the same roadmap outcome.

items.says: The checkout-test achievement repeats an earlier bullet.
items.because: It duplicates the account of the same work.

items.says: Define what the five-point lift measures.
items.because: The description of the test result needs precision.

items.says: Explain why the lift is described as an effect on merchants’ customers.
items.because: The claimed effect needs a precise interpretation.

items.says: Make the relationship between your presentation and the funded rollout precise.
items.because: The reader will want to know your role in securing the decision.

items.says: Specify what the leadership team funded.
items.because: The scope of the funded rollout is unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether you owned subsequent rollout work.
items.because: The bullet does not establish your role after the funding decision.

items.says: Clarify the timeframe behind the nine tonnes of food.
items.because: The impact figure needs a clear period.

items.says: Clarify your role in the launch if others contributed.
items.because: The bullet should establish your individual contribution.

items.says: Define weekly active users and the before-and-after periods.
items.because: The growth result needs measurement context.

items.says: Check the causal link between the interviews and reminders.
items.because: The review says the link should be accurate.

items.says: Clarify the timeframe of the fill-rate change.
items.because: The before-and-after figures do not state a period.

items.says: Describe the change as a 20-percentage-point increase if that is what is meant.
items.because: The stated movement is from 75% to 95%.

items.says: Make your contribution to the volunteer system clear.
items.because: The bullet does not fully establish your individual role.

items.says: Distinguish the modeled saving from realized savings.
items.because: Funding a pilot does not establish that the savings were achieved.

items.says: Replace the passive construction with a clear account of your contribution.
items.because: It obscures who mapped intake and shortened the form.

items.says: Say what improved when the intake form was shortened.
items.because: The bullet does not give a measurable result, if there was one.

items.says: The pilot approval repeats an outcome in the savings bullet.
items.because: The two bullets appear to recount the same client decision.

items.says: Add substantiated product skills relevant to the posting.
items.because: The current skills list is thin for product roles.

items.says: Show relevant analytical or technical tool depth where accurate.
items.because: The section gives little evidence of that depth.

items.says: Clarify proficiency and how the listed tools were used.
items.because: Bare tool names do not show whether they supported analysis, tracking, experimentation, or coordination.
